title: Business Card Size: 3.5×2 in, 85×55 mm, Bleed & 300 DPI
h1: Business Card Size, Bleed and Print Resolution
description: US business cards are 3.5×2 in; Europe often uses 85×55 mm. Bleed, safe zones, 300 DPI pixel sizes, landscape layout, and matching your printer template.
summary: In the US and Canada the usual trim size is 3.5×2 inches; in much of Europe it is 85×55 mm. Add bleed (0.125 in or 3 mm) so color reaches the edge after cutting, keep text inside the safe area, and export at 300 DPI for print.

sections.heading: Standard trim sizes at a glance
paragraphs: Trim size is the finished card after the printer cuts the sheet. US and European cards use different proportions, so pick the region where you will print.
after: 85×55 mm is slightly taller relative to width than a US card. A design composed for 3.5×2 in will need re-layout or scaling for strict 85×55 mm output, not a silent stretch.

sections.heading: Bleed, trim and safe zone
paragraphs: Bleed is extra artwork beyond the trim line so a small cut error does not leave a white hairline. US shops commonly ask for 0.125 in bleed on all sides; many European templates use 3 mm per edge.

The safe zone is the inner area where text and logos should stay so they are never trimmed off. Printers publish their own templates; a typical rule is to keep important content at least 3 mm (about 0.125 in) inside the trim.

PiCraft keeps contact type inside a centered safe rectangle on the card front. If you edit the file afterward, respect the same margins. For why bleed exists, see [what is bleed in printing](/blog/what-is-bleed-in-printing).

Printers do not all use the same numbers. VistaPrint's standard US card template is 3.61×2.11 in with bleed and a 3.36×1.86 in safe area, which is a thinner bleed than 0.125 in. An Irish online printer, WePrint.ie, asks for 3 mm of bleed and important content at least 5 mm inside the final cut. The PiCraft US file is 3.75×2.25 in. If your printer's template is smaller, place the file centered and trim the extra from each edge (0.07 in per side for the VistaPrint size) instead of scaling it.

sections.heading: Resolution, orientation and color
paragraphs: Print shops expect 300 DPI for crisp small type. The pixel sizes in the table above come from multiplying the bleed dimensions by 300 (for example, 3.75×300 = 1125 px width for US bleed width).
Business cards are almost always designed in landscape orientation: the long edge runs horizontally when you hand the card to someone with the text right-side up.
Card stock weight (for example 14 pt or 16 pt) affects feel and thickness but not the digital file size. Choose stock with your printer; the PDF dimensions stay the same.

Many printers ask for CMYK files. VistaPrint and WePrint.ie both say so, and VistaPrint recommends a print-ready PDF. PiCraft's print PDF and JPG are RGB; the maker does not convert them to CMYK. Printers usually convert on their side, so expect saturated screen colors such as bright blues and greens to look slightly duller on paper, and order a proof if a brand color matters.

sections.heading: How to check your printer's template
paragraphs: Before you order, download the template from your print vendor (Vistaprint, Moo, a local shop, or an online PDF spec). Open it in the tool they recommend and compare trim, bleed and safe guides to your file.
Confirm whether they want a single front PDF with bleed, a flattened JPG, or separate front and back files. Upload the PDF with bleed unless they specify otherwise.
If the template trim size differs from 3.5×2 in or 85×55 mm, do not force-fit your art. Resize the canvas to their trim and adjust the layout, or pick a printer that matches the size you designed.
items: Download the printer's PDF or PNG template for your chosen size.
Place your artwork on the front layer and align trim and bleed guides.
Verify phone numbers, email and URLs character by character.
Order a small test batch or a PDF proof if the shop offers one.

sections.heading: Web preview size vs print file
paragraphs: A lower-resolution JPG is useful for email signatures and social profiles; it is not a substitute for the print PDF. PiCraft exports a web JPG near 1050×600 px for US cards and 1020×660 px for European size, plus 300 DPI print files with bleed.
The maker designs the front only. Backs are often a solid brand color or a logo added in the printer's editor. It does not embed QR codes or uploaded logos in the generated front.

sections.heading: Make a card at the right size
paragraphs: The [Business Card Maker](/create/business-card-maker) lets you choose US & Canada (3.5×2 in) or Europe (85×55 mm) and downloads a print PDF and 300 DPI JPG with bleed, plus a web JPG.

For other print pieces at Letter size, see [flyer size](/sizes/flyer-size). Invitations and related specs live under [invitations and print](/categories/invitations-and-print). To test a file you already have for bleed and resolution, use the free [image size checker](/tools/image-size-checker).

faq.q: What is the standard business card size in the US?
faq.a: 3.5×2 inches is the usual trim size in the United States and Canada. Print files include 0.125 inch bleed on each edge (3.75×2.25 in total).

faq.q: What size is a European business card?
faq.a: 85×55 mm is the common trim size in much of Europe, with 3 mm bleed per edge (91×61 mm total) on many templates.

faq.q: How many pixels is a business card at 300 DPI?
faq.a: With bleed, about 1125×675 px for US size and about 1075×720 px for 85×55 mm European size at 300 DPI.
Landscape is standard: text reads horizontally when the card is handed over with the long edge on top.

faq.q: Do I need bleed if I print at home?
faq.a: Home printers often cannot print full bleed. For professional trimming at a print shop, use a file with bleed so backgrounds reach the cut line.

faq.q: Can one file work for US and EU sizes?
faq.a: No. The proportions differ. Design or export separately for the region where you will print.

faq.q: Is business card bleed always 0.125 inch?
faq.a: No. 0.125 in (3 mm) is the common figure, but templates differ. VistaPrint's standard US card is 3.61×2.11 in with bleed, which is about 0.055 in per edge. Use the template for the exact product you order.

faq.q: Do I need to convert the file to CMYK before printing?
faq.a: Check with your printer. VistaPrint and WePrint.ie ask for CMYK. PiCraft exports RGB, so ask whether the shop converts RGB files or wants you to do it, and request a proof for colors that matter.
